examples.question: If I walk to the round table, then look back to face where I come from, which direction would have the most open space?

topdown.title: ADDITIONAL TOP-DOWN MAP
topdown.caption: Numbered markers show the start (0) and successive movement positions. Lines show the path; the final arrow shows the final facing direction. Use this map together with the START and FINAL VIEW RGB images.

text.title: ADDITIONAL TEXT TRAJECTORY
text.text:
The description gives the movement and camera turns from start to final state. Turns are relative to the current view, and view tilt is relative to level. Use it together with the START and FINAL VIEW RGB images.
Begin at the position and viewing direction shown in the starting image. Use that starting direction as 0°. All left and right turns below are relative to your current view.

Your initial view is level.

Step 1: Raise your view by 0.1° so it is 0.1° above level. Move forward 3.23 m to the next position, keeping that viewing direction during the movement. After arriving, turn right 12.1° in place.

Step 2: Keep your current viewing direction. Move forward 2.88 m to the next position, keeping that viewing direction during the movement. After arriving, turn around 180.0° in place and lower your view by 0.1° so it is level.

Stop here. You have traveled 6.10 m in total across 2 movement segment(s). You are now facing 167.9° to the left of your starting direction, with your view level.

video.title: ADDITIONAL TRAJECTORY VIDEO
video.caption: The video shows the movement from start to the final state, including camera turns. Translation uses discrete connectivity hops. Use it together with the START and FINAL VIEW RGB images.

depth.title: ENDPOINT DEPTH MAP (same camera pose and field of view as FINAL VIEW)
depth.caption: Colors encode camera-forward distance (z-depth), not object color. Red/orange is nearer, green is intermediate, and blue/purple is farther; black means missing depth, not a nearby surface. This image's color scale runs from 2.120 m (near/red) to 8.095 m (far/purple), with values outside this range clipped. Combine this map with START and FINAL VIEW RGB to reason about the final state.

surface_normals.title: ENDPOINT SURFACE NORMAL MAP (same camera pose and field of view as FINAL VIEW)
surface_normals.caption: Colors encode surface orientation, not object color or distance. RGB channels encode normal components along camera-right (R), camera-up (G), and camera-forward (B): 0 = -1, about 128 = 0, and 255 = +1. Higher R/G/B means a stronger rightward/upward/forward component; a surface facing the camera has low B. Black means missing geometry. Combine this map with START and FINAL VIEW RGB to reason about the final state.

panorama.title: ENDPOINT PANORAMA (360-degree RGB at the FINAL VIEW position)
panorama.caption: The panorama is centered on the final camera's facing direction. At mid-height, the center is forward, one-quarter of the width is left, three-quarters is right, and the two joined edges are behind. Top/bottom look up/down; colors are natural RGB, not geometric labels. This is one position, not a sequence of movement frames. Combine it with START and FINAL VIEW RGB to reason about the final state.
